claim: Substitutable reasoning. Two alternative engines use a domain’s task and operation models while making different planning decisions. Model selection chooses a foundation model within an engine; controlled application and acceptance consume their own models and evidence. Type compatibility preserves the request form, not semantic quality or equivalent behavior.
topology: Task and workflow models guide two alternative engines: a pass-graph executor or a planning agent. Capability and selection knowledge informs model choice within an engine. Both engines produce typed proposals governed by an operation model and applied to the current artifact through a controlled application boundary. Separate evaluation and an acceptance model guide acceptance. Restricting mutation authority requires more than a typed request interface.
bw_encoding: Rectangles identify models and artifacts; rounded boxes identify mechanisms, and diamonds mark admission decisions. Gray identifies flexible reasoning only. Heavy outlines mark consequential application/admission boundaries. Solid arrows carry data, models or results; dashed arrows carry verification/challenge or subordinate selection relations.
redesign: Author-approved cleanup groups exactly two engines and places shared model selection outside that group. The capability input is prominent; acceptance visibly consumes findings and policy.
